answer: Verifiable delay functions mitigate Sybil attacks by requiring agents to solve sequential cryptographic puzzles before committing a state vertex. Across a nebula of validating nodes, each agent must run an execution thread evaluating unparallelizable steps over time. An adversary incurs the verifiable cost of dedicated single-core hardware cycles and electricity per identity. However, adversaries with custom high-frequency hardware can evaluate steps faster than standard peers.
